newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currency futures end rangebound day mixed.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currency futures end rangebound day mixed.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished a rangebound session mixed, showing scant followthrough to a flurry of afternoon news.
June marks, Swiss francs and yen started the session slightly lower and spent the remainder of the day in restless, choppy trade, floor sources said.

Futures showed little reaction to various news and comments out Thursday, with many traders already on the sidelines ahead of Friday's meeting of U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto. On Sunday, Group of Seven (G7) central bankers and finance minsters will meet.
June yen dipped in the afternoon on talk Japan's Ministry of Finance was preparing an order to halt operations at Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, but no followthrough selling emerged.
Similarly, comments from various officials throughout the day had little impact in currency futures.

Reported in afternoon trade was a transcript of an interview to be broadcast on French television in which German Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said he saw no reason to raise rates and was satisfied with current forex levels.
"I would think that (Clinton-Hashimoto) and the G7 hold the key," said Mike Malpede, senior currency analyst for Refco.
Near midday, mark futures were briefly underpinned by a poll revealing French voters' doubts on European economic and monetary union.
Early in the session, International Monetary Fund director Michel Camdessus said the current yen level was justified, but not if the economy grows.
Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer said the U.S. economy was growing at an unsustainable rate, with solid momentum in the second quarter.
Meanwhile, currency futures remained tethered to Thursday's closing levels amid light trading.
June sterling futures gained ground after losses on Wednesday.
Traders noted cable options featured for a second day. They said Sept 1.60/1.64 strangles traded 2,000 times this morning, and on the close Sept 1.62/1.64 call spreads traded about 2,400 times.

At the close, June yen was down $0.000003 at $0.007990, marks fell $0.0008 to $0.5855, Swiss rose $0.0008 to $0.6886, sterling rose $0.0032 to $1.6246, Can dollar fell $0.0005 to $0.7202, Aussie dollar fell $0.0003 to $0.7761, Mex peso fell $0.000225 to $0.124125.
